title: Reuters reports hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform; attackers and scope unknown
date_note: The pages give only their own publication day, 27 November; they say the breach was discovered about a month earlier during a system update.
geo_basis: country: the platform belongs to the US Air Force, no city is stated
summary: Reuters, citing anonymous sources, reports hackers breached the Air Force's Cloud One platform, found within roughly the past month during an upgrade. One source said the intruders exploited a software flaw to reach the control plane; scope, data theft and attacker are unknown. NBC News reports a US official confirmed the breach but gave no timing or impact. The Air Force said it does not comment on the security posture of specific networks.
plain: Reuters, citing anonymous sources, reports that hackers got into the US Air Force's main cloud platform. Some work on it was paused. Reuters could not say who did it or whether data was taken.
exec: Reuters reports a breach of an Air Force cloud platform that paused migrations and updates; the Air Force declined to comment, and scope and attacker are unknown.

validation.note: Two publishers, Reuters (kelo.com) and NBC News (nbcmiami.com), each state the breach; NBC says a US official confirmed it to NBC. Both rely on unnamed sources; the Air Force declined to comment on specifics. Staradvertiser answered 403.

review.note: title, date, discovery timing, control-plane claim, Air Force comment against KELO/Reuters and TNW
